_about: Ruling 220 (log b352, b359): each country's ladder of air formation names with the real strength of each rung in aircraft, by the historian (historian/air-formation-names-220.json, 17 November 2026). An air group takes, once, as it is formed, the name of the rung nearest its full strength: near is between half and twice the rung's strength, the nearest by ratio; where no rung is near, the plain form of airwar.json's groups.names._default. Tokens: {n} the number, {nth} the English ordinal, {n+K} the number plus K, {nth_fr} the French ordinal (1re, 1er before a régiment), {nth_nl} the Dutch (1e). Rows with from or until (months from 1, September 1939) hold only then; rows 'in exile' hold only while the country's homeland is lost, and then only they. Japan: JAP_navy for groups based on the provinces named in navyBases (none on the map yet), JAP elsewhere.
_airNames: The switch 'airNames' (release 2; the design director's ruling of 25 November 2026 03:18Z, design-director/air-names-1125.md; src/campaign/air.ts groupName). Off, nothing below this note is read and every group is named as ruling 220 names it. On, a new group still takes, once, the rung nearest its full strength, but the words change: (a) 'numbers' on a rung, for fighters and for bombers, are the numbers that arm really used, handed out in the order the game forms its groups; when a list runs out the series goes on from the next whole number above the largest handed out, never one a group of that nation already carries. An empty or missing list numbers that rung as ruling 220 does (1, 2, 3, ...). A number is a label only. The rows 'in exile' are rungs of their own, so they keep lists of their own; the Guards series is in nicknames.json (air, guards). (b) 'formR2' on a rung replaces its 'form' under the switch (the role in the name where the arm said it there); where a form reads the same for fighters and bombers the name does not say the role, and the page and the card show it beside the name. 'short' on a rung is the form for the map counter (for example 'JG {n}'); 'skipIfTaken' (Germany's Gruppen) passes over a Gruppe label whose Geschwader number a Geschwader-size group of the same side already bears. A list may hold whole labels ('I./JG 26', 'II/5') where the arm wrote its units so; past the end such a list goes on in its own manner. (c) 'navyIslands' are the provinces whose groups are Japan's navy's under the switch (the historian's suggested split in air-formation-names-220.md: the Marianas, Carolines, Marshalls, Solomons and Bismarcks, as the map draws them); its groups there take the airfield's name ({base}) at forming and keep it for life; a second group formed at a base that already names one takes Japan's navy's numbered fallback (the record's numbered group; the rule is G). 'navyStations' would map a province to the record's station name; it is empty, so {base} is the province's name. 'fallback' is each arm's own plain form where no rung is near; for an arm without one the switch takes the nearest rung of its own ladder however far, so that no arm reads another country's word, and only a nation with no ladder at all keeps airwar.json's English plain form. 'blocked' lists real air units' names and honour titles that no name of ours may hold (checked by tests/air-names-r2.test.ts with nicknames.json's list). The 'numbers' lists, 'formR2' forms, 'short' forms, 'fallback' forms and the 'blocked' list are the historian's (historian/air-unit-names-r2.json and .md, 25 November 2026 03:40Z), laid in as read; most number lists are marked M there (real numbers in near forming order, labels only), and the fallbacks of arms without their own are G. The 'short' forms await the UI director. (Italy's day-one names were dropped by Brian's answer of 03:31Z: its wind and myth words are its earned list, nicknames.json air.styles.italian.)

blocked._note: Real air units' names, nicknames and honour titles that no name of ours may hold, matched as whole words (the historian's 'blocked', air-unit-names-r2.json, 309 names, all arms, Italy's air division names of June 1940 among them; and two more, Sirio and Zeffiro, that are the air thread's own, added on 25 November: 311); and one more, Death Rattlers, a real squadron's nickname added by the air thread on 25 November after the design director's review marks of 05:12Z ("Rattlers" was struck from our American names as too near it): 312 in all. Over-blocking does no harm. A place of this war in one of our names (a Guards city, a place name: the group's own latest hard fight) is not refused merely because one of its words is a distinctive word of a blocked name (the design director, 12:59Z question 6: a place word is the war's own map, not a nickname's mark); the rest of the name is still checked word by word, and the whole name, place included, is still tested against every blocked whole name, so a place that is itself a blocked name (Moscow) never stands in a name. This list holds no real Guards honour titles by number, place and arm together; the whole-name test covers only what is listed here and in nicknames.json 'blocked'.
blocked._common: The words of a blocked name that are NOT its distinctive words (the design director's review marks of 05:12Z: the block test also catches a real nickname's distinctive word, not only the whole string). A blocked name's distinctive words are all its words (letters and digits, an apostrophe kept inside a word: Hell's) but these, matched whole and without regard to case; a word made only of digits is a number and never distinctive. No name of ours, generated or listed, may hold a distinctive word of any name on this list or on nicknames.json 'blocked' (airnames.ts airBlocked; tests/air-names-r2-words.test.ts). What is here, the air thread's first cut for the historian to edit: articles and small words in the languages of the list; the plain colours, and gold and silver; the two the ruling names, Flying and Fighting; numbers in words; the words that say what kind of formation or aircraft a unit is (Air, Force, Wing, Squadron, Group, Division, Brigade, Corps, Army, Regiment, Bomber, Fighter, Command, Kommando, Jagdverband), which our own formal names must use; one word of nationality, American; and the points of the compass and 'old' (North, South, East, West, Old: added after the review of 25 November, as words of places, East India, West Riding, Old Hickory, rather than of a nickname's mark). Everything else is distinctive: Iron, Devils, Lightning, Sky, Sea, Bell, Watch, Thunder, Hill, High, Boys and Tin among them, so names of ours that held them were replaced (nicknames.json air.styles).

UK._roleNumbers: Release 1.5.2: the record numbered Britain's groups by role (the historian's read row, historian/air-names-roles-1125.md section 4, 25 November 2026 13:04Z, mark L): a new fighter group takes the first free number of its list, a new bomber group of its. 'abroad': a number the record gave another country's group (No. 6 to Canada), last in its list and taken only while no living air group of any nation carries it ('so leave 6 to Canada while Canada holds it'). Where a kind's list runs out, the next name takes the lowest whole number above every number in both lists that is free: never a number of the other kind. (Release 2: read only by ruling 220's names, with the switch 'airNames' off (air.ts groupName); 1.5.2 kept these lists under 'numbers', which on this line is the switch's own forming-order list above, so they stand here under a key of their own.)

navyStations._note: The record's named navy air stations (the historian, air-unit-names-r2.json navyBases.JAP.record) by the chart province each stands in: a navy group forming in such a province takes the station's name, one forming elsewhere its province's chart name. EMPTY: no navy group forms in the home islands, Formosa or Korea under ruling 220's split (navyIslands), so no station has been mapped; the historian's list is Yokosuka, Tainan, Kanoya, Takao, Genzan, Mihoro, Chitose, Misawa, Kisarazu, Toko, Yokohama, Atsugi, Kasumigaura, Takuma, Bihoro, Saeki, Kure, Sasebo, Omura, Iwakuni, Oita, Usa, Suzuka, Tsukuba, Hyakurihara, Konoike, Ominato, Maizuru, Chinkai.
